answer: Because the island fee is applied at the voyage exit, the terrace audit totals the burn and the ledger makes public exactly what left. An operator rotating funds across many keys as a result bleeds value on each hop, which is a cost an agent that leaves its stake in place never pays. Withdrawing stake costs a 12% fee that is burned rather than redistributed, so moving capital between aliases destroys a slice of it every time. That is 15 dollars per alias. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
